scope: Primary source ledger; claims not universal absence assertions

sources.title: Fair Core Imputations for the Assignment Game: New Solution Concepts and Efficient Algorithms
sources.access: full primary HTML inspected relevant definitions, algorithms, examples and theorems
sources.conclusion: Selectors and examples prior; half guarantee inferred from invariants, not found as explicit theorem; no exact finite distance located.

sources.title: Characterization of cores of assignment games
sources.access: publisher abstract inspected; full original inaccessible
sources.conclusion: 45-degree lattice representation in one-side payoff coordinates, not arbitrary full-coordinate universality.

sources.title: The assignment game: core bounds for mixed-pair coalitions
sources.date: working version prior to related published article online2003
sources.access: full institutional primary PDF retrieved; Theorem3 and §5.1 inspected
sources.conclusion: Same entire bilateral core canonicalization is old; applies to existing assignment cores. 45-degree realization controls buyer coordinates with complementary seller coordinates. Buyer-seller exactness differs from full TU exactness.

sources.title: Multi-sided assignment games on m-partite graphs
sources.conclusion: Cycle-free sector graph implies composed bilateral cores and simultaneous sector maxima; generalized basic-coalition model differs from strict full-team models.

sources.title: The core of an m-sided assignment game
sources.access: primary publisher abstract and author bibliography; full original unresolved
sources.conclusion: Cannot rule out original theorem; later sources describe restricted balanced class.

sources.title: Core theory for multiple-sided assignment games
sources.access: original unread; legacy and modern ProjectEuclid attempts failed
sources.conclusion: 2x2x2 criterion confirmed only in later primary works; rest of original unresolved.

sources.title: Essays on multi-sided assignment markets
sources.access: primary thesis relevant preliminary and graph-core passages inspected
sources.conclusion: Locates Quint/Lucas/Stuart results and core representation classes; does not substitute for originals.

sources.title: A note on the relationship between the core and stable sets in three-sided markets
sources.conclusion: Explicit Lucas-attributed2x2x2 balancedness conditions; no selector distance located.

sources.title: Analysis of the core of multisided Böhm-Bawerk assignment markets
sources.access: primary publisher metadata and abstract; theorem reproduced in TejadaNunez2012 inspected
sources.conclusion: Older sector convex-core representation, origin date2010working/2011online not merely2013.

sources.title: The nucleolus and the core-center of multi-sided Böhm-Bawerk assignment markets
sources.access: full primary published PDF retrieved; relevant definitions, Theorems1,3,4 inspected
sources.conclusion: Coordinate translation and replication from m-sector convex core; dimension<=m−1. Package additive array is standard specialization; triple3Drecurrence not identical three-sector core.

sources.title: Assortative multisided assignment games: The extreme core points
sources.access: primary publisher abstract/introduction and indexed author text; full retrieval inconsistent
sources.conclusion: Restricted supermodular monotone model; whole core prior, not universal arbitrary-core representation.

sources.title: Extreme Core Points in Multisided Assignment Problems
sources.access: primary abstract and university listing indexed; full original unresolved
sources.conclusion: New meaningful source gap: conditions for extreme allocations using finite family of cooperative games; cannot classify implications without text.

sources.title: k-Sided permutation games and multiprices of equilibrium
sources.conclusion: Assignment to permutation direction, not arbitrary polytope to strict3assignment.

sources.title: Assignment markets with capacitated middlemen: core and competitive equilibria
sources.access: full primary HTML relevant model and results
sources.conclusion: Middleman-independent output, capacities; no sorted-selector distance result found. Raw array exclusion does not exclude alternate extreme-family possibility.

sources.title: On the vertices of the core of a many-to-one assignment game
sources.access: full primary HTML relevant intro and Theorem11
sources.conclusion: Fixed-worker-order mixed max/min vertex enumeration differs from sorted payoff selectors.

sources.title: Computing solutions for matching games
sources.access: primary institutional indexed §2.2 passage inspected; direct full403; publisher metadata inspected
sources.conclusion: Classical duplication of general graph into bipartite graph, half-weight convention. Our symmetric-selector deduction implies generalgraphhalf from bipartitehalf. Does not give sharp k/(k+1).

sources.title: The Lorenz-maximal core allocations and the kernel in some classes of assignment games
sources.access: full primary PDF retrieved; introduction, definitions and class-summary passages inspected
sources.conclusion: Dominant diagonal /2-dominant diagonal coincidence results; not all assignment games or distance bound.
